chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Singing 'Mississippi' for Rock and White
summary: After a tape change, Whaley retells how he sang the talk-song 'Mississippi' from Rock and White's show when they visited Suntaug Lake Inn and they sent him $200.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: We're going to start again. I'd like to change tapes for just a minute here, right in the middle of that beautiful story you were telling about these celebrities you played for. Now what about Rock & White?

Well, Rock & White played--they had a show downtown, see. And I used to tell the guys, "hey, you better go down there and see this show." So, I went down to see it and they had a number in there called "Mississippi" (spells it out). "That used to be so hard to spell, it almost made me cry." Well, you know, I loved that number, and the waiter--one night--the waiter came over and says...
Now, this is in this club? The waiter was in this club you were working?
What's the name of this club again?
Yeah. Outside of Wakefield. Lynnfield, Massachusetts.
And all the celebrities used to come there for dinner?

Yeah, after--we used to work from seven til twelve. The waiter come over and said, "There's a party over there, Rock & White. They want to know if you know any music from the show." I said, "see! I told you they'd be down here!" So I said, "Yes, I know 'Mississippi'."
So I sang it, or talked--it was a talk-song.... a lisp. (sings) "M-I-Sth-Sth-I-Sth-Sth-I-P-P-I, That used to be so hard to spell, it almost made me cry." And I sang the whole thing through.
(above portion not picked up by transcriber)
You know what they did? They sent me $200 -- and I said to the guy, I said, "See that? I shouldn't give you guys any of this."
